LOOK: Catholic faithful, led by the Clergy for Good Governance, holds a procession which began and ended in Edsa Shrine on Sunday to call for accountability amid a multibillion corruption scandal involving flood control projects. 

The solemn protest action was held concurrently with the Feast of Christ the King, or the last Sunday which marks the end of the current Catholic liturgical cycle.

The new liturgical year begins on Nov. 30, which also coincides with another massive nationwide protest action as part of the Trillion Peso March which began in Sept. 21. | via @JEMendozaINQ

Akbayan Party today joined Filipino laypeople and clergymen at the EDSA Shrine for the Centennial Celebration of Christ the King, a gathering led by the Clergy for Good Governance (CGG), to protest the worsening corruption in government, demand an end to political dynasties, and call on citizens to join the sequel of the Trillion Peso March. 

Echoing the spirit of the growing “No Kings” protests in the United States, where citizens reject authoritarianism and hereditary entitlement. Akbayan stressed that Filipinos, too, must reject any attempt to turn public office into a family crown.

Akbayan President Rafaela David emphasized that corruption in the Philippines survives because it is protected by political dynasties that treat public office as inherited property. “Akala ng mga dinastiya sa Pilipinas ay mga hari sila, at ang posisyon sa gobyerno ay minana nila at ipinamamana pa nila. Panahon nang tapusin ang paghahari-harian ng iilang mga pamilya sa ating bayan. Ibalik ang kapangyarihan sa taumbayan!” David said.
